reading.body:
Robert Wittman's AI record in this data is mostly money: ten PAC contributions from Amazon, Anthropic, Palantir, Intel, Oracle, and Google, plus four recorded votes on bills.

The contributions run from February 2025 to August 2026 and total $24,000. Amazon gives the most, $12,500 across four payments, including the largest single check, $5,000. Palantir and Google each appear twice. The donors are the companies that build or sell AI compute and the software layered on it, which is why the pattern matters here: the same firms whose data centers and chips set the pace of AI scaling are also writing checks to the members who vote on the rules around them.

The votes are thinner than the money. Four recorded votes appear, three Yea and one Absent, and the data gives bill numbers without saying what the bills do. Nothing here establishes that any contribution preceded or influenced any vote, and the page states plainly that placement in date order is not a claim of causation.

What this does not cover is as important as what it does. There is no spending total for the cycle, no opponent, no committee assignments, and no text of the bills. A reader can see who gave and when, and how one member voted on four occasions, and nothing more than that.
